title: Field Maple: Ancient Field Maples You Can Visit
meta_description: Europe's hedgerow maple, rarely singled out. Four mapped: a Prague garden veteran near 170 years, a Graz maple already noted protection-worthy in 1956.
intro: Field maple is the tree that fills gaps between hedgerows rather than anchoring a park, which is exactly why the four mapped here stand out from their own species. Prague's, in the Seminary Garden above a pond, carries the group's most precise age, estimated at 160 to 170 years. Graz protects two: one on the wooded Schlossberg hill with no recorded age at all, and one in the Augarten already listed as protection-worthy in a 1956 survey, decades before its formal 1979 designation, giving it a documented floor of at least seventy years. Lisbon's, in Parque Bensaude, has no dated record either. Acer campestre rarely gets a second look; these four earned protection or a place on this map anyway.
